problem:
Let $v$ be a non-zero vector from ${R}^{2}$ and let $A$ be the rotation-scaling matrix given by

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3\sqrt{2} & -3\sqrt{2} \\ 3\sqrt{2} & -3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}].
$$

The description of $Av$ in terms of geometric transformations in the plane is given below. What are the missing entries?

*To compute the vector $Av$, we rotate $v$ counterclockwise by an angle of $\theta =\text{_____}$ and then scale the result by a factor of $r=\text{_____}.$*

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14094884/assets/a42ab3804fa207390da60307a2af967d075c0ae7d1dd108f6db809540ffa6e6a.png)

The vectors $v$ and $Av$ are shown above. If $A$ is a rotation-scaling matrix, then $A=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $A$ is a rotation-scaling matrix, then we can write

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}r & 0 \\ 0 & r\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}],
$$

where $r$ is the scale factor and $\theta $ is the angle of rotation. 

According to the diagram, $r=\frac{1}{3}$ and $\theta =-\frac{3\pi }{4}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}r & 0 \\ 0 & r\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{3} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} & \frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} \\ -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6} & -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{6}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
